userStories.title: Move token-answering invites to gate-secret and add wait-policy fixtures
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Reserve secret-bearing invite routes for the secret rollout and supply a reusable agent wait-policy fixture.

**Motivation** — The medium-risk writes still bypass the engine on REST.

**Approach** — **The two token-answering invite routes are `gate-secret`.** This applies the 5b ruling ("a route whose answer is a token or secret shown once") to `POST /projects/:slug/invites` (its `INVITED` outcome carries `invitePath` with the raw token) and `POST /projects/:slug/invites/:id/resend` (it rotates the token and answers it). `DELETE /projects/:slug/invites/:id` answers nothing secret and is gated here. Here refers to this feature: US-009 gates invite.cancel; US-001 only classifies the deferred token-answering routes.

**A test helper seeds the wait.** `seedWaitPolicy(db, key, projectId)` (in `approvals/test-helpers/approval-fixtures.ts`) upserts, on `selector`, the `ApprovalPolicy` row `{ selector: '<projectId|*>|<key>|type:AGENT', projectId, permissionPattern: key, principalType: 'AGENT', mode: 'agent', updatedByType: 'SYSTEM', updatedById: 'test' }` (the shape `assistant-direct-action.integration.spec.ts` writes inline) and answers `{ id }`. `selector` is unique, so an upsert lets two tests of one file seed the same key. The resolver reads policies per request (no cache), so no invalidation is needed.

US-001: `SECRET_GATE_ROUTES` gains `POST /projects/:slug/invites` and `POST /projects/:slug/invites/:id/resend`, and their `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES` rows are relabelled `gate-secret`. The rollout rule in `expectedPendingGateRoutes` already checks `SECRET_GATE_ROUTES` first, so it needs no change.

**Each gating story removes its own `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES` rows**, as in 5b. US-001 relaxes the exact gated-route count to a lower bound (at least 41), and US-011 restores an exact count (62).

**Scope** — In: pending-gate-routes.ts, permission-contract.spec.ts (eight secret labels), approval-fixtures.ts, a new seed-wait-policy.integration.spec.ts, and the temporary lower-bound/title change in permission-contract.integration.spec.ts. Out: actual route gating belongs to US-003–US-010; final exact counts and OpenAPI belong to US-011. Gating the 8 `gate-secret` routes, including the two invite routes moved here.

**Interface** — `seedWaitPolicy(db, key, projectId)`; answers `{ id }`. Accept the existing fixture DB/transaction shape and projectId null for global policies. Use the exact selector and row fields above. New DB fixture tests must be independent, delete policies/decisions/requests before each test, and run under the shared DB gate, not require DB in unit tests.

userStories.title: Compare only the tested VCS target during settlement (#346)
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Stop benign polling writes from failing approved VCS connection tests while retaining target, token and row-identity fencing.

**Motivation** — #346 is bundled into this spec.

**Approach** — **#346: settlement compares the tested target.** `prepareTestConnection` snapshots `{ id, provider, repoOwner, repoName, encryptedToken }` of the connection it tested, and settlement compares the same snapshot of the re-read row with `isDeepStrictEqual`. A missing row, a replaced row (new `id`), or a change to any of those fields throws `ValidationAppException({}, 'vcs')` as today. Changes to `lastSyncedAt`, `updatedAt`, `syncMode`, `pollingIntervalMs`, `allowedAuthors`, `webhookSecret` and `isActive` no longer fail it.

**Scope** — In: existing vcs-connection.service.ts, vcs-connection.service.spec.ts, and gated-webhook-vcs-routes.integration.spec.ts. Keep the existing repoName-changed unit regression. Add one it.each row for repoOwner/provider/encryptedToken, and gone/replaced-row assertions. Cross the vcsTestTarget -> prepareTestConnection settlement -> rest:vcs.test seam with GitHubProvider.prototype.testConnection writing lastSyncedAt before returning { ok: true }. Out: ticket/domain gates are other stories. US-002 only: changing what `testTarget` checks, or moving the provider call inside the approval transaction.

**Interface** — `vcsTestTarget(connection)` in `vcs/vcs-connection.service.ts` (module function, exported; not the private method `testTarget`, which runs the provider call): `{ id, provider, repoOwner, repoName, encryptedToken }`.
`VcsConnectionService.prepareTestConnection(projectId, encryptionKey)`.
Settlement target: `isDeepStrictEqual(current && vcsTestTarget(current), vcsTestTarget(connection))`. Preserve the callback's provider result and existing failure exception; do not put credentials in approval input/result. No new files. The integration test uses the already-shipped high-risk VCS gate and approval policy defaults, with isolated request/decision/policy cleanup and restored provider spy.

userStories.title: Gate ticket create, update and assign REST writes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Apply approval policies to ticket creation, update and assignment through REST variants while retaining immediate default behavior.

**Motivation** — A project owner who sets `ticket.* → agent` for agents makes the assistant and MCP tools wait, while the same agent calling `POST /projects/:slug/tickets` or `koda ticket create` writes at once.

**Approach** — Each row is one `routeCommand`. "Scope" is the `projectId` passed to `ApprovalRouteGate.run` (`null` = global; "project" = `@CurrentProject()`'s id). The run calls the service the handler calls today, with `principal` the rebuilt `UserPrincipal | AgentPrincipal`. Every body-returning command declares `toResult: (result) => result` unless the row says otherwise; a no-body command declares none. On `executed` the handler answers `JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result)` with the route's status, as today.

| Route | Key | Scope | Variant | Input | Run |
| POST /projects/:slug/tickets | ticket.create | project | rest:tickets.create | `{ slug, ticket: parseBody(CreateTicketDto, …) }` | `tickets.create(slug, ticket, principal)` |
| PATCH /projects/:slug/tickets/:ref | ticket.update | project | rest:tickets.update | `{ slug, ref, patch: parseBody(UpdateTicketDto, …) }` | `tickets.update(slug, ref, patch, principal)` |
| POST /projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/assign | ticket.assign | project | rest:tickets.assign | `{ slug, ref, assignee: parseBody(AssignTicketDto, …) }` | `tickets.assign(slug, ref, assignee, principal)` |

- Id and string members are read with `parseRouteInput` (5b). A body member is read with `parseBody` of the route's DTO; a missing body member is parsed as `{}`.
- **Only the HTTP handlers change**, as in 5b. The controllers' helper methods (`createTicket`, `updateTicket`, `assignTicket`, `verifyTicket`, …, `CommentsController.create`/`update`, `LabelsController.create`/`update`/`assignLabel`) and their spec cases stay.
- **The gate key is the route's key, not the ticket's edge key.** Two inputs move a ticket along an edge another route owns: `PATCH …/tickets/:ref` with a `status` (gated under `ticket.update`; the service then checks the edge key), and `POST …/verify` on a VERIFY_FIX ticket (gated under `ticket.transition.verify`; the service closes it through the `verify-fix.approve` edge). A policy on the edge's key does not make these two wait; a policy on the route's key does. Gating them by the effective edge would need the ticket read before the gate and is out of scope.

**Scope** — In: extend TicketRouteCommands/TICKET_ROUTE_VARIANTS preserving delete, gate the three HTTP handlers with @ApprovalGated while retaining @Requires/@ApiResponses/parameter lists, remove exactly their pending rows, update commands/controller specs and create gated-ticket-write-routes.integration.spec.ts. Change permission-contract.spec.ts's old ticket-create allowlist anchor to POST /memory. The gate is already injected; no module import changes. Controller assign handler assertions become gate assertions, create/update gain cases, and service-call expectations live in commands specs. Out: transitions belong to US-004/005 and final counts/OpenAPI to US-011; do not gate status patches under the service edge's key.

**Interface** — `ApprovalRouteGate.run({ key, variant, projectId, input, keyCheck? })`, `routeCommand(spec, loader)`, `parseBody`, `parseRouteInput`. Handler shape:
```ts
const outcome = await this.routeGate.run<TicketResponseDto>({ key: 'ticket.create', variant: TICKET_ROUTE_VARIANTS.create, projectId: project.project.id, input: { slug, ticket: dto } });
if (outcome.status === 'pending') throw new ApprovalPending(outcome.request);
return JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result);
```

**Test setup** — Agent has project.read, ticket.create, ticket.update and ticket.assign in P, no transition key; grantKeys then PermissionCache.invalidate. Seed the route's wait policy per waiting test using seedWaitPolicy; no policy means immediate execution with no request. Direct root still executes with no request under a policy. Each AC owns its rows and repeats prior-call setup when approving; delete every ApprovalPolicy plus decisions/requests in beforeEach, and use the DB gate. Approved service refusals retain failed result `{ error: 'execution-failed', name }`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] POST /api/projects/:slug/tickets by the agent under a wait policy returns 202 with data matching { permissionKey: 'ticket.create', projectId: P }.
AC-2 [integration] Approving the agent's pending ticket create leaves one ticket with that title whose createdByAgentId is the agent.
AC-3 [integration] Approving the agent's pending PATCH /api/projects/:slug/tickets/:ref { title: 'renamed' } leaves the ticket titled 'renamed'.

AC-4 [integration] Approving the agent's pending PATCH /api/projects/:slug/tickets/:ref { status: 'IN_PROGRESS' } on a CREATED ticket settles the request failed (the agent holds no edge key), with result { error: 'execution-failed', name }.
AC-5 [integration] Approving the agent's pending POST /api/projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/assign { agentId: <the agent's id> } leaves assignedToAgentId equal to the agent.
AC-6 [integration] POST /api/projects/:slug/tickets by the agent with no policy seeded returns 201 and writes no ApprovalRequest row.
AC-7 [integration] POST /api/projects/:slug/tickets with the root token under a wait policy returns 201 and writes no ApprovalRequest row.
AC-8 [unit] After onModuleInit, the registry returns ticket.create, ticket.update and ticket.assign commands for rest:tickets.create, rest:tickets.update and rest:tickets.assign.

AC-9 [unit] The registered rest:tickets.assign command's execute calls tickets.assign('alpha', 'AL-1', { userId: 'cuser1' }, <principal>) for parsed input { slug: 'alpha', ref: 'AL-1', assignee: { userId: 'cuser1' } }, where principal is returned by the loader (the route specification's run callback).
AC-10 [unit] TicketsController.create calls routeGate.run with { key: 'ticket.create', variant: 'rest:tickets.create', projectId: <the project id>, input: { slug, ticket: <the dto> } }.

userStories.title: Gate ticket verify, start and fix transitions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Route initial ticket workflow transitions through approval without moving body or service validation boundaries.

**Motivation** — Any policy now applies on REST the same way it does for assistant and MCP writes.

**Approach** — **A transition command answers the ticket.** The services answer `{ ticket, comment?, activity }`; the handler answers `result.ticket`. The command's run answers `result.ticket`, so `ApprovalRequest.result` and the executed body are the ticket the route answers today.

| Route | Key | Scope | Variant | Input | Run |
| POST /projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/verify | ticket.transition.verify | project | rest:tickets.verify | `{ slug, ref, body }` | `(await transitions.verify(slug, ref, body, principal)).ticket` |
| POST /projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/start | ticket.transition.start | project | rest:tickets.start | `{ slug, ref }` | `(await transitions.start(slug, ref, principal)).ticket` |
| POST /projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/fix | ticket.transition.fix | project | rest:tickets.fix | `{ slug, ref, body }` | `(await transitions.fix(slug, ref, body, principal)).ticket` |

Request checks the handler makes before its service call stay before the gate, so they answer as today and open no request: the comment-body check of verify, fix, verify-fix, close and reject (`requireCommentBody`, 400 `tickets`). Every check inside a service (edge keys, transitions, conflicts, row ownership) runs when the command runs, at once or after approval; a failing check settles the request `failed`. This is 5a's rule. Under a policy, an edge-key refusal or an invalid transition therefore answers 202 first and fails at execution.

Id and string members are read with `parseRouteInput` (5b). The transition `body` member is a required non-empty string (`parseRouteInput(input, ['slug', 'ref', 'body'])`).

**Scope** — In: extend TicketRouteCommands with TicketTransitionsService injected after TicketsService, add verify/start/fix variants and identity toResult, gate only their HTTP handlers after applicable body checks, retain existing parameter order/Requires/ApiResponses and add @ApprovalGated, remove the three pending rows. Update commands and HTTP-handler unit specs (including existing start and verify cases) and create gated-ticket-transition-routes.integration.spec.ts. Preserve helper-method specs and previous variants. Out: verify-fix/close/reject belong to US-005; final exact counts/OpenAPI to US-011. POST verify on VERIFY_FIX is gated by ticket.transition.verify, not the effective edge key; changing that rule is out of scope.

**Interface** — `TicketTransitionsService.verify/fix/close/reject(slug, ref, body, principal)`, `.start(slug, ref, principal)`, each answering `{ ticket, … }`. `ApprovalRouteGate.run({ key, variant, projectId, input, keyCheck? })`; set projectId to project.project.id, freeze the table inputs, throw new ApprovalPending(outcome.request) on pending and return JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result) on executed.

**Test setup** — Agent holds project.read plus ticket.transition.verify/start/fix in P. Root prepares each ticket's required status, each waiting test seeds its route-key policy, and each AC creates independent rows and repeats the pending call it approves. Delete every ApprovalPolicy/ApprovalDecision/ApprovalRequest before each test, reset throttle and invalidate PermissionCache after grants. Service refusal after approval must expose failed with `{ error: 'execution-failed', name }`, not a pre-gate domain error.

AC-2 [integration] After independently repeating AC-1's request, before approval, the ticket is still CREATED.
AC-3 [integration] Approving an independently created AC-1 request leaves the ticket VERIFIED with a comment whose body is 'ok'.
AC-4 [integration] Approving the agent's pending POST /api/projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/start on a VERIFIED ticket leaves it IN_PROGRESS.
AC-5 [integration] Approving the agent's pending POST /api/projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/fix { body: 'fixed' } on an IN_PROGRESS ticket leaves it VERIFY_FIX.
AC-6 [integration] POST /api/projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/verify { body: '  ' } by the agent under a wait policy returns 400 and writes no ApprovalRequest row.
AC-7 [integration] Approving the agent's pending verify after root verified the ticket while it waited settles the request failed, with result { error: 'execution-failed', name }.
AC-8 [unit] After onModuleInit, the registry returns commands for rest:tickets.verify, rest:tickets.start and rest:tickets.fix under their respective transition keys.

AC-10 [unit] The rest:tickets.fix command's parse({ slug: 'alpha', ref: 'AL-1' }) throws ValidationAppException with key 'approvals.invalidInput'.

userStories.title: Gate ticket verify-fix, close and reject transitions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate remaining ticket transitions, including permission-key selection for approve versus return.

**Motivation** — Any policy now applies on REST the same way it does for assistant and MCP writes.

**Approach** — **verify-fix gates the key its `approve` flag needs.** The route accepts either verify-fix key (`mode: 'any'`). The handler gates `ticket.transition.verify-fix.approve` when `approve` is `true` (or `'true'`) and `ticket.transition.verify-fix.return` otherwise. Each key registers its own command under the same variant `rest:tickets.verify-fix`; the `.approve` command calls `verifyFix(…, true, …)` and the `.return` command `verifyFix(…, false, …)`, so the input carries no flag. A caller holding only the other key gets 403 `permissions` from the route gate (today the service's edge check answers the same 403).

- The verify-fix handler validates the body, reads `approve` as today, then gates `{ key: approve ? '…verify-fix.approve' : '…verify-fix.return', variant: 'rest:tickets.verify-fix', projectId, input: { slug, ref, body } }`.
- **A transition command answers the ticket.** The services answer `{ ticket, comment?, activity }`; the handler answers `result.ticket`. The command's run answers `result.ticket`, so `ApprovalRequest.result` and the executed body are the ticket the route answers today.

| Route | Key | Scope | Variant | Input | Run |
| POST /projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/verify-fix | ticket.transition.verify-fix.approve (when approve) | project | rest:tickets.verify-fix | `{ slug, ref, body }` | `(await transitions.verifyFix(slug, ref, body, true, principal)).ticket` |
| (same route) | ticket.transition.verify-fix.return (otherwise) | project | rest:tickets.verify-fix | `{ slug, ref, body }` | `(await transitions.verifyFix(slug, ref, body, false, principal)).ticket` |
| POST /projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/close | ticket.transition.close | project | rest:tickets.close | `{ slug, ref, body }` | `(await transitions.close(slug, ref, body, principal)).ticket` |
| POST /projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/reject | ticket.transition.reject | project | rest:tickets.reject | `{ slug, ref, body }` | `(await transitions.reject(slug, ref, body, principal)).ticket` |

**Scope** — In: the existing ticket commands/controller and their specs; register four commands under three variants, preserve previous registrations, remove three HTTP-route allowlist rows, create gated-ticket-review-routes.integration.spec.ts. Keep @Requires mode any for verify-fix, all existing path/query/principal/project parameters in order, @ApiResponses, and helper methods. Add @ApprovalGated and preserve requireCommentBody before every gate. Existing close handler body cases assert gate calls; existing verify-fix/close blank-body unit cases still throw before gate and stay. Out: initial transitions belong to US-004; contract totals/OpenAPI belong to US-011. Do not freeze approve in input or treat two keys as two HTTP routes.

**Interface** — `TicketTransitionsService.verifyFix(slug, ref, body, approve, principal)`, `.close(slug, ref, body, principal)`, `.reject(slug, ref, body, principal)`. Parse required transition strings using `parseRouteInput(input, ['slug', 'ref', 'body'])`; use identity toResult, project.project.id for scope, ApprovalPending on pending, and JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result) on executed.

**Test setup** — Each independent AC binds only its route's key plus project.read, invalidates PermissionCache, seeds that key's wait policy, and has root prepare a ticket at the appropriate status. Each AC approving another AC's request repeats its own call and rows. Delete all ApprovalPolicy/ApprovalDecision/ApprovalRequest rows before each integration test. A blank body still gives 400 tickets with no request; missing selected key gives 403 permissions with no request. Service failures remain deferred failed results, not new handler prechecks.

userStories.title: Gate comment creation and ownable updates
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Apply approval policies to comment create/update while retaining slug-less lookup privacy and row ownership rules.

**Motivation** — The medium-risk writes still bypass the engine on REST.

**Approach** — The comment update handler calls `resolveCommentProject(id, principal)` first, then gates with `projectId` its answer (as the 5b delete handler does). `comment.update` is ownable, so the route gate accepts `comment.update.own`; the row-level check runs in the service.

Request checks the handler makes before its service call stay before the gate, so they answer as today and open no request: the comment's project lookup of `PATCH /comments/:id` (`resolveCommentProject`, 404 `comments`), which the gate needs for its scope. Every check inside a service (edge keys, transitions, conflicts, row ownership) runs when the command runs, at once or after approval; a failing check settles the request `failed`.

| Route | Key | Scope | Variant | Input | Run |
| POST /projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/comments | comment.create | project | rest:comments.create | `{ slug, ref, comment: parseBody(CreateCommentDto, …) }` | `comments.create(slug, ref, comment, principal)` |
| PATCH /comments/:id | comment.update | the comment's project (resolveCommentProject) | rest:comments.update | `{ id, patch: parseBody(UpdateCommentDto, …) }` | `comments.update(id, patch, principal)` |

**Gated handlers keep their existing parameters, in order.** Unlike 5b, a handler keeps a `@Principal()` parameter it no longer reads (oxlint's `no-unused-vars` is off). A handler that needs the project and has no `@CurrentProject()` today appends `@CurrentProject() project: ProjectContext` as its last parameter: comments `createFromHttp`. Route parameters always stay declared, so the OpenAPI document keeps every path parameter.

**Scope** — In: extend CommentRouteCommands/COMMENT_ROUTE_VARIANTS preserving delete; gate createFromHttp/updateFromHttp with @ApprovalGated and existing Requires/ApiResponses; add CurrentProject only to createFromHttp; drop their two pending rows, update commands/controller specs and create gated-comment-write-routes.integration.spec.ts. Keep CommentsController.create/update helper methods and their spec cases. The module already has the gate/auth wiring.
